reading.body:
Equinix DC22 in Ashburn is one building in the largest data center metro on the continent, spanning 15 facilities across four locations from Ashburn to Culpeper County in Northern Virginia. The operator publishes no megawatt figure for this specific facility, making its individual weight on the grid unknowable from public sources. The campus as a whole anchors the major peering point between North America and Europe, but that scale is distributed across the metro, not isolated in this building.

Virginia holds 1,375 megawatts of published data center capacity across 23 facilities with disclosed figures. DC22 does not rank among them individually; it is either smaller than the 23 published sites or the operator chose not to disclose its power draw on its product page. Among the 326 mapped facilities statewide, the vast majority also publish nothing, leaving the true load geography of the state substantially opaque.

Equinix states 100 percent renewable energy coverage for DC22, meaning the power it consumes will be matched with renewable attributes under the operator's procurement strategy, though the actual grid electrons serving the facility remain determined by Virginia's generation mix. No redundancy or cooling specifications are published on this facility's page. The absence of a megawatt figure is the binding fact; without it, the question of whether this campus matters to AI scaling cannot be answered from Equinix's own disclosures.
